prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on your needs — surgical placement vs. final crown, complexity of the case, budget and whether you want a specialist. I can help find specific providers if you tell me your ZIP code and any preferences (insurance, sedation, weekend appointments). Meanwhile, here’s a quick, practical guide to find the best dentist for a dental implant in Denver and what to look for.

1. Choose the right provider type
- For implant surgery (placement): look for an oral and maxillofacial surgeon or a periodontist. They do most implant surgeries and complex grafting.
- For the implant restoration (crown/bridge): a prosthodontist or an experienced general dentist who does implant prosthetics.
- For single-source care: some practices provide both surgery and final restoration in-house.

2. Key credentials and experience to prefer
- Board certification (for oral surgeons: American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery; for periodontists: American Board of Periodontology is relevant).
- Years of implant experience and implant volume (how many implants placed per year).
- Training in advanced procedures: bone grafts, sinus lifts, guided/3D implant surgery.
- Use of CBCT (3D imaging) and digital implant planning.
- Fellowship, university appointments, or professional lecturing / published research are pluses.

3. What patients often value
- Before/after photos and case examples (especially for complex cases).
- Clear implant brand(s) used and warranty/guarantee policy.
- Sedation options (IV sedation, nitrous).
- Transparent pricing and financing options.
- Good patient reviews and responses to complications.

4. How to vet local providers in Denver
- Search Google Maps, Healthgrades, Zocdoc, Yelp and read both good and bad reviews.
- Look up the provider on state dental board to confirm licensure and disciplinary history.
- Check the practice website for CBCT, 3D-guided surgery, and team bios.
- Call for a consultation and ask targeted questions (see next section).

5. Questions to ask at a consultation
- Who will place the implant and who will restore it?
- How many implants have you placed? How many similar to my case?
- Do you use CBCT and do you do guided implant surgery?
- What implant system do you use and why?
- Do I need bone grafting or a sinus lift? How do you manage those?
- What sedation options are available?
- What is the total cost (surgery + implant + abutment + crown) and financing?
- What are your complication rates and how are complications handled?
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references?

6. If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of highly reviewed oral surgeons / periodontists / prosthodontists in Denver if you give your ZIP code or neighborhood and any preferences (insurance or price range).
- Draft phone/script questions to call clinics.

Tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and any priorities (insurance, timeline, sedation) and I’ll build a tailored short list.
